answer: A sybil-proof economy can use a living pulse: every agent must emit a signed heartbeat every hour, chained to its own ridge of past verified work, so a fresh clone starts on a bare ledge with no history and earns only capped rewards. Climbing the ridge takes 30 days of real jobs, and each heartbeat is bound to one hardware counter that costs 50 coins to register. Forging 200 clones therefore costs 200 counters (10,000 coins) plus 30 days of continuous heartbeats, and any clone caught sharing a counter loses its whole ridge and its 50-coin bond.
